source.title: Discovering Forbidden Topics in Language Models
source.authors: C. Rager; C. Wendler; Rohit Gandikota; David Bau

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how forced thought suppression affects refusal propensity, using logit differences and a refusal count. This is a different measurement of a prefill intervention than the claim’s harmful-completion bypass test.
record.gate_note: The paper uses prefilling to discover refused topics and reports topic-recovery coverage across prompt-injection locations. Those coverage results measure the crawler’s discovery performance, not whether harmful user requests receive compliant answers, so they are not rows for the claim versions. The study does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, fine-tuning erosion, safety-localized parameters, or safety deepening.
record.test_reason: The study uses prefilling as the engine of a refusal-discovery crawler (IPC) and reports the crawler's topic recall and coverage. It never measures how often a prefilled compliant opening makes a model comply with harmful requests. Figure 2's Tiananmen example of prefilling breaking refusal is a single qualitative illustration. The thought-suppression experiment forces an empty reasoning block and measures increased refusal on benign queries. That is the reverse intervention, not V4's bypass of refusal, so no row bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors conclude that prefill-based crawling (IPC) can discover refused topics: 31/36 Tulu-3 topics, recall 0.83 vs 0.77 for the baseline. DeepSeek-R1-70B shows CCP-aligned censorship with thought suppression. Thought suppression correlates strongly with refusal; its causal effect on refusal rates is small (3/100), though the logit ratio suggests some causal influence. A key conclusion the record omits: the 8-bit quantized Perplexity-R1-1776 model reinstates CCP refusals that the bf16 version lacks, so audits must target deployed models.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses prefill-based topic crawling and forced thought suppression, not fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement as in the cited original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: For topic discovery, the thought-prefix injection location yields the broadest topic coverage among the tested locations; this is crawler coverage, not a harmful-compliance measure.

fits_no_version.finding: In DeepSeek-R1-70B, forcing an empty reasoning block (thought suppression) raises the Sorry-vs-Okay logit ratio to S=3.43±1.21 on 100 benign queries. Greedy decoding gives 3/100 refusals. Thought suppression appears in 0.96 of refusals, with 0.60 precision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prefilling a refusal-style opening (empty chain of thought) in reasoning models raises refusal likelihood even on benign queries. The opening positions steer refusal in both directions.

record.problems: The refusal-rate result is on benign queries and does not report an explicit clean-condition count; the logit ratio is a proxy rather than a harmful-completion rate. The text describes the causal impact on refusal rates as limited.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant behavioural rows. Topic-recovery and prompt-location coverage results are excluded because they measure discovery performance rather than harmful-request compliance.

untested.parts: No benign fine-tuning. The quantization effect on the Perplexity model is not fine-tuning.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No measured rate of harmful compliance under compliant prefills, suffixes or decoding changes. Prefill is used only as a crawler tool, plus one qualitative example (Fig. 2).
No analysis of the cause of shallowness. Authors state IPC cannot identify the source of refusal.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 'tests V4' assignment and its limits_scope label are dropped. The rows measure refusal induction on benign prompts, not refusal bypass on harmful prompts. Injection-location topic coverage (Table 3) measures crawler performance and is correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
The study tests forced thought suppression on benign queries, not compliant openings on harmful requests, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes; it does not report harmful completion rates.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
Training safety beyond the opening tokens and its robustness.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-70B
rows.stage_stated: reasoning model; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Forced thought suppression (TS) before the response; compared logit differences on clean and suppression datasets.

conditions.value: greedy sampling for the refusal-rate result

rows.measure: Ratio S of the logit difference (Sorry minus Okay) on the suppression dataset to that on the clean dataset, measured after </think>.
rows.baseline: 1 (ratio indicating no increase in refusal likelihood)
rows.note: The authors say S > 1 indicates increased refusal likelihood and interpret this result as TS influencing refusal tendencies. This is a logit-based likelihood measure on benign queries, not a harmful-completion rate; it cannot establish the bypass behavior specified by V4.
rows.check: Forced empty <think></think> on benign queries raises a Sorry-vs-Okay logit ratio (S=3.43±1.21). This measures refusal induction by a prefilled opening, not bypass of refusal on harmful requests, so it does not measure V4's effect.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-R1-70B
rows.stage_stated: reasoning model; training stage not stated
rows.operation_detail: Forced TS and measured the model’s refusal count on benign queries using greedy sampling.
rows.note: The queries were selected because they did not trigger refusal otherwise, but the text does not state an explicit clean-condition refusal count. This benign-query count does not measure compliance with harmful requests.
rows.check: 3/100 benign queries refused under forced thought suppression. The clean baseline is implicitly 0, since queries were chosen not to trigger refusal. This is refusal induction on benign prompts, not harmful-request compliance after a compliant prefill.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Forced thought suppression on 100 benign queries
reader_labels.reason: The tested intervention and prompts do not establish that compliant openings bypass refusals on harmful requests: the actual refusal count was 3/100, and the reported logit ratio is not a harmful-completion rate (R1, R2).
